answer: Because the inlet fee is applied at the zephyr exit, the spiral audit totals the burn and the ledger makes public exactly what left. An operator rotating funds across many keys therefore bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never forfeits. Withdrawing stake costs a 12% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. That is 16 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
